items.title: kaizen:backlog → Claude Code TaskList auto-sync (no roundtrip)
items.probe: kaizen-backlog add/start/tick/park automatically reflects into the active CC TaskList (subject/description/status), so the agent doesn't need separate TaskCreate calls
items.verify: Hook layer that bridges backlog state changes to the CC task surface. Two directions: (a) on 'kaizen-backlog add', emit a TaskCreate equivalent via a SessionState-aware mechanism (file watcher or daemon tick) so the next agent prompt picks it up; (b) on 'kaizen-backlog tick/done', emit TaskUpdate completed. Constraints: CC TaskList lives in-harness, not on disk — so the bridge needs either a CC SDK hook OR a marker file the agent loads on next prompt. Likely shape: write to .kaizen/inbox/backlog-task-events.jsonl, then UserPromptSubmit hook surfaces unprocessed events as 'pending task suggestions' for the agent to ack with TaskCreate calls. Integration test asserts add-then-prompt surfaces the suggestion.

items.title: kaizen — project vs global metadata scope discipline (audit + lint)

Lint catches features that write to the wrong scope (e.g. project-scoped data leaking to global path).
items.verify: (a) Survey existing persisted-state features (backlog, handoff store, brain, dxm, trace, gold, intent, inbox) — document scope for each in a domain/state-scopes.yaml lens manifest. (b) Add iron-law: every script that writes state must resolve its path via _paths.py and the path must be tagged project|global in the manifest. (c) BK-023 ledger declares scope=project (per-repo memory dir, NOT default/memory). (d) Integration test: feature writes go to the declared scope only — no cross-scope bleed.
